classification.difficultyReason: Read non-negative or negative intervals from supplied cubic graphs, including repeated roots.

content.prompt: Solve these cubic inequalities by referring to the given graph.

spec.description: Cubic with roots 0, 1 and 3, labelled x-axis ticks 1, 2 and 3; origin numeral omitted by house convention. Source red curve uses standard red.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph remains visible; solution intervals appear only in answers.

answer.worked:
The graph is above the $x$-axis for $0<x<1$ and $x>3$. Include the intercepts because the inequality is $\ge0$.

$0\le x\le1$ or $x\ge3$.

spec.description: Cubic crossing at -3, one half and 2. Fractional-root arrow retained. Positive y-intercept corrected to 6. Origin numeral omitted.

answer.worked:
The graph is below the $x$-axis to the left of $-3$ and between $\frac12$ and $2$. Exclude all intercepts because the inequality is strict.

$x<-3$ or $\frac12<x<2$.

spec.description: Negative-leading cubic with root arrows at minus square root of 3 and square root of 3, crossing also at 1. Negative x-axis tick corrected to -1. Origin numeral omitted.

answer.worked:
The graph is above the $x$-axis for $x<-\sqrt3$ and $1<x<\sqrt3$. Include the three intercepts because the inequality is $\ge0$.

$x\le-\sqrt3$ or $1\le x\le\sqrt3$.

spec.description: Cubic crosses at 1, touches at 2 and has marked y-intercept -4. Marked roots retained; origin numeral omitted.

answer.worked:
The graph is on or above the $x$-axis for every $x\ge1$. At $x=2$ it touches the axis and remains non-negative.

$x\ge1$.

spec.description: Cubic touches the x-axis at the origin from below and crosses at 4. Both intercept points marked; origin numeral omitted.

answer.worked:
The graph is below the $x$-axis for $x<4$, except at $x=0$, where it touches the axis. Exclude both $0$ and $4$ because the inequality is strict.

$x<0$ or $0<x<4$.

spec.description: Cubic touches at -1 and crosses at 3. Marked y-intercept corrected from -8 to -6. Origin numeral omitted.

answer.worked:
The graph is below the $x$-axis for $x<3$, except at $x=-1$, where it touches the axis. Exclude both intercepts because the inequality is strict.

$x<-1$ or $-1<x<3$.
